title: Slice-aware kernel adapter + prefill/decode scheduler for mixed-MIG H100 and L40S fleets
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce 95th percentile token latency for customer workloads running on mixed MIG/HW fleets by selecting attention kernels and clock targets dynamically based on active MIG slice size and real-time power headroom.

Background: We have several customers running inference across heterogeneous nodes (H100 1g/2g, L40S, A10) with multiple MIG partitions active. Static kernel selection and a single prefill/decode scheduler do not fully utilize the headroom available on higher-clocked slices and over-throttle larger partitions, causing unfair latency distributions and wasted cycles.

Scope and deliverables:
- Implement a "slice-aware kernel adapter" in the serving runtime that: 1) queries GPU topology and active MIG slice size, 2) chooses an attention kernel variant (fused-unfused, tiled vs streaming, int8 vs fp16) and micro-batch size informed by slice compute and ECC, 3) annotates chosen kernel metadata for tracing and cost accounting.
- Extend prefill/decode scheduler to consider per-slice clock governor and recent power telemetry so decode tasks can opportunistically run on higher-clock slices while prefill uses larger partitions when available.
- Add a runtime flag (RUNTIME_MIG_ADAPT=1) guarded rollout and a Canary policy for dedicated pools.
- Benchmark harness and dashboards: add per-slice p95/p99 metrics, kernel-selection breakdown, and token cost delta chart.

Acceptance criteria:
- 95th percentile token latency reduced by >=10% on target mixed-cluster perf tests (see benchmarks).
- No regressions for tail latency on small-slice workloads (within ±3%).
- Traces show kernel metadata and selected clock target for >=90% of requests in canary pools.

Notes about constraints and trade-offs:
- Using per-request clock steering can increase host-side scheduling complexity and may slightly reduce throughput for very large batches. We will only steer clocks for latency-sensitive routes and maintain a throughput-preserving fallback policy.
- Not all kernels are numerically identical across data types; we need eval prompts to ensure output quality is preserved when switching to more aggressive int8 kernels.

comments: 2026-02-22 — Priya Patel: Initial spike completed. Profiling on H100 1g vs 2g shows ~18% faster fused-attn kernel on 2g for seq_len=1024 with batch 4, but 2-3ms jitter on small slices under contention. Collected traces and kernel heatmap. Saved artifacts to the design doc.

2026-02-28 — Marco Chen: Implemented kernel adapter prototype that exposes KernelVariant enum and per-slice scoring function. Hooked scoring into dispatcher; added unit tests for scoring edge-cases. PR opened: #5492. Running cluster canaries on staging-dedicated.

2026-03-03 — QA (Anika Rao): Early canary results: p50 unchanged, p95 improved 9% on mixed-H100 test but small-slice customers saw a 2.6% latency increase for cold-starts. Added regression prompts to perf-suite; scheduling tweak planned.

2026-03-06 — Marco Chen: Added backpressure limiter for slice-steering when power headroom < 12W to avoid thermal throttling. Also added explicit fallback to stable kernel variant for non-latency routes.

2026-03-09 — Performance Eng (Diego Morales): End-to-end benchmark run 2026-03-08 attached in dashboard. Observed 12.4% p95 reduction for target routes on L40S/H100 mix with RUNTIME_MIG_ADAPT=1. Throughput held within 1.8% for bulk decode workloads.

2026-03-12 — Priya Patel: Preparing rollout notes and runtime flag gating. Need PM sign-off on release messaging and decide on canary pool size. Open question: whether to expose an opt-in console toggle per-customer initially. Assigned to PM for decision.
